import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Grimm's conjecture

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grimm%27s_conjecture)
-/

open Function

namespace Grimm

/--
**Grimm's Conjecture**
If $n, n+1, \dots, n+k-1$ are all composite numbers, then there are $k$ distinct primes $p_i$
such that $p_i$ divides $n + i$ for all $0 \le i \le k-1$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem grimm_conjecture (n k : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (hk : 1 ≤ k)
    (h : ∀ i : Fin k, (n + i).Composite) :
    ∃ ps : Fin k ↪ ℕ,  ∀ i : Fin k, (ps i).Prime ∧ ps i ∣ (n + i) := by
  sorry

/--
**Grimm's Conjecture, weaker version**
If $n, n+1, \dots, n+k-1$ are all composite numbers, then their product
has at least $k$ distinct prime divisors.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem grimm_conjecture_weak (n k : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (hk : 1 ≤ k)
    (h : ∀ i : Fin k, (n + i).Composite) :
    ∃ ps : Fin k ↪ ℕ,  ∀ i : Fin k, (ps i).Prime ∧ ∃ j : Fin k, ps i ∣ (n + j) := by
  sorry

end Grimm

reformulations.difference: Instead of counting the distinct prime divisors of the product, Lean requires an injective family of k primes, each dividing some member of the composite block.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The product P of the block is nonzero. For any prime p, p divides P if and only if it divides at least one factor. Consequently, the required embedding Fin k ↪ ℕ exists exactly when k ≤ P.primeFactors.card. The source’s one-based block is obtained by shifting the starting parameter; its positive-integer convention also makes “no prime in the interval” equivalent to all entries being composite. Both the product-count equivalence and the full equivalence with this interval formulation were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, without using either conjecture theorem or sorry.

review.notes: Both declarations faithfully state their source claims. Nat.Composite means 1 < n ∧ ¬Nat.Prime n, and the nonempty composite-block hypothesis forces the starting value to be at least 4. Thus the positivity bounds and indexing shift introduce no discrepancy. The embedding correctly enforces distinct primes. Both research-open tags agree with Wikipedia’s explicit unproved status. Scratch proofs checked reindexing, empty and singleton cases, and the concrete block 8,9,10. Computational tests found no failures for either formulation among 486 admissible blocks with 1 ≤ n ≤ 200 and 1 ≤ k ≤ 10. The final scratch and test files compile successfully.
